items.html: When blurred, the standard Kazakh licence plates are mostly white, with a small hint of blue on the left side.

Kazakhstan uses both Cyrillic and Latin alphabets.

Though sometimes, Russian is used monolingually.

  • The following letters are found in the Kazakh but not Russian alphabet: Ә (Ä), Ғ (Ǵ), Қ (Q), Ң (Ń), Ө (Ö), Ұ (W), Ү (Ü), Һ (H), І (I).
  • Kazakh is related to Turkish, so the Latin text can appear similar.
All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.

Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.

Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.

Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings. However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side. Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.

Street Signs in Kazakhstan are often attached to buildings and are blue in colour, with white intricate patterns on the top and bottom. They are usually bilingual or trilingual and can also contain a QR code.

NOTE: They are often inconsistent, with many designs being found in a single city.

Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards. Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.

The bottom of tree trunks are very often painted white.

NOTE: This is common in several eastern European countries, as well as in parts of Russia.
Unlike neighbouring countries, Kazakhstan primarily uses yellow and black chevrons, except on T Intersections, where you will find the more generic red and white chevrons.
Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.
This ornamental pattern known as the koshkar-muiz can be found as part of decorations in all kinds of settings in Kazakhstan.
Many cities and towns in Kazakhstan have these entrance arcs, which are often quite intricate and ornate.

Coverage in Kazakhstan is fairly limited. While most major roads and cities are covered, coverage on small rural roads is fairly uncommon. As such, knowing which roads have coverage can help narrow down the guess.

Kazakhstan can easily be divided into coverage regions based on the season.

  • Summer in western and central Kazakhstan.
  • Autumn in the northeast.
  • Winter in the southeast.
Driving directions can help you narrow down your options when you are on a rural road.
Kazakh area codes are useful to learn, and they generally follow an east to west pattern along three horizontal lines.

You can occasionally spot licence plate codes on the back of trucks and buses. The codes themselves follow an alphabetical order, with smaller numbers corresponding to regions that start with earlier letters. Note that cars do travel, and as such not all codes are reliable. Buses and smaller utility vehicles are the most reliable.
While rarely possible, being able to read the letters under a QR code on a street sign will give you the region.

Kazakhstan is a generally flat country, so getting locations that are hilly or mountainous are useful for narrowing the options.

For example, the region around Karaganda is often either quite hilly, or you can see hills in the distance.

Another notable set of hills would be the ones around Aktobe.

And of course getting bigger mountains will mean you are in the south, or east.

These lush birch forests next to green fields are common in northern Kazakhstan.

NOTE: This landscape often appears very similar to that found in and around Omsk Oblast in Russia.
Vast grassy green plains are found in northwestern Kazakhstan. They are especially common in Akmola and Kostanay regions.
Sandy and shrubby desert-like landscapes are common in southwestern Kazakhstan.
Tall mountains, which are often snow-capped, can be seen in southeastern Kazakhstan.
The East Kazakhstan Region is hilly and forested. It was covered in october, so you will see fall colours on the vegetation. The town of Ridder itself is flat, but surrounded by hazy mountains.
Snow coverage can be found in southeastern Kazakhstan, especially east of Almaty.

The landscape in southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan is hilly and quite dry and shrubby, with a lot of orange looking grass. The landscape consists of dry but grassy rolling hills or dead flat agricultural land near Zhetisay.

NOTE: These red and white KM markers that look like Kyrgyz ones, are only found near Zhetisay.
Grassy green rolling hills can be found in southern Kazakhstan. They are especially common just north of Bishkek.
Around Semey, you can find small clusters or entire forests consisting mostly of pine trees and some deciduous trees, which will have fall colours.

The divided section of the E38 goes southeast to northwest from Shymkent to Kyzylorda. The road is made of asphalt, and it has all white road lines. The landscape varies quite a lot; in the south, it is very green and in the north, it gets dry, sandy, and shrubby.

Driving direction: Both ways

The section of the M36 going from Karaganda to Almaty can often be recognised by the road being under construction, with a second lane being built. Yellow lines are common. As for the landscape, it’s a wintery dry steppe, which looks noticeably orange-brown.

Driving direction: South from Karaganda.

Between Karaganda and Astana, the M36 is now a divided highway, with yellow outer lines. The landscape consists of a grassy, sometimes hilly, steppe with an occasional row of trees along the road. Note that the general southeast to northwest road angle is important.

Driving direction: Both ways

The P4/A17 from Astana to Pavlodar is a divided road, generally going east to west, through a hilly steppe landscape similar to the M36, but is generally less vegetated. Most of the road has outer yellow lines.

Driving direction: Both ways

The roads from Kyzylagash to Druzhba feature a unique hilly landscape, which looks hazy and dead. On most sections, you will see small mountains either south or east of the road.

Driving direction: East from Kyzylagash.

The A26 goes from Kandyagash to the intersection of M32/E38.

It has very bad road quality throughout, ranging from poor grainy pavement, to completely unpaved. Apart from the northernmost section, the weather is either cloudy or overcast.

The landscape consists mostly of flat, semi-arid grassy plains.

Driving direction: North towards Kandyagash. (Mostly)

The section of the A1 going from Astana to Shchuchinsk is a 6-lane divided highway. The landscape around is generally quite green, with trees and grassy plains or hills.

Driving direction: Both ways

The A17 going to Ulytau Region can be recognised by the bad pavement quality, where the edges of the road are almost crumbling away, along with the single white middle road line, which can be dashed or solid. The landscape itself is a grassy steppe, with some fall coloured trees occasionally lining the roads.

West of Atasu, the sun is distinctly low on the horizon.

NOTE: A small section east of Atasu has pristine new pavement, which has a slight red tint to it.

Driving direction: Towards Atasu from both directions

The road north of Zhezqazghan has no road lines. The landscape is very dry, desolate, with very limited vegetation and slightly hilly. The soil can look very red or orange at times.

The weather is sunny, with a lot of cumulus clouds.

Driving directions: North from Nikolskiy

The R260 road is mostly paved, but not in the best condition; many cracks can be seen, and it mostly lacks road lines. The weather is overcast and the landscape is a slightly hilly steppe, consisting of somewhat yellow grass and reddish soil, which is very evident when the road is unpaved.

The R217 is very similar, but the road is in better condition and mostly has very faded dashed white middle road lines, which are often quite difficult to see. The further east you go, the more sparse the cloud cover gets.

Driving directions: South from Atbasar

These regions/cities have the most useful pole paints you can learn.

The descriptions will be written from top to bottom:

  • West Kazakhstan Region uses red, white, and black paint.
  • Atyrau Region uses blue, white, and black paint.
  • Akmola region has a very thin layer of red, then white, and a thin layer of black on the bottom.
  • Kostanay uses a thin layer of turqoise, and yellow.
  • Petropavl has a thin layer of white, and light grey.
  • Taraz has red, yellow, and black.
  • Kyzylorda poles have a thin layer of yellow and red, then white.
  • Kyzylorda lamp posts are white, and have turquoise on the bottom.

These pole paints are less useful than the above hint, but still worth learning if you want to master Kazakhstan.

The descriptions will be written from top to bottom:

  • Rudny has red, yellow, red on the top, with white below it.
  • Kokshetau uses a few designs, but they all have light blue on the bottom, and sometimes, a thin strip, or two, of yellow on top.
  • Shchuchinsk has a thin layer of red, and yellow.
  • Ekibastuz has a thin layer of blue, and white
  • Shymkent poles have a thin layer of yellow and red, then green.
  • Kentau poles have thin layers of blue, yellow, and red, then blue and black below them.

These are the most useful to learn bus stops.

  • Atyrau has a modern design, with white and lime/neon green walls. The bus stop name is prominently written on top.
  • Kostanay uses simple brown bus stops, that have a blue and yellow crest on one of the glass panes.
  • Petropavl also has brown bus stops, with glass panes on all 3 sides not facing the road. The roof is angled slightly upwards.
  • Karaganda uses old looking turquoise bus stops, which have a curved roof.

Zhezqazghan has very wide blue bus stops, which have 2 sections; 1 indoors, and one outside. These sections are separated by a door.

These cities have buses worth learning.

  • Aktobe uses orange and black buses.
  • Zhezqazghan has orange and white buses, with “Men ♥ Jezz/Zhez” written on the sides.
  • Astana commonly uses these white, black, and green electric buses.
  • Karaganda uses turquoise buses, just like their bus stops.
  • Semey has these light green and white buses.
  • Almaty uses fully green buses, with white patterns and the city name on the sides. Taraz can use similar buses, but they will have “Taraz” written on the sides instead.

These street signs attached to buildings are generally quite inconsistent, but there are some worth knowing.

  • Aktobe has compact signs where half of the space is taken by the QR code.
  • Petropavl uses white signs, with a blue semicircle below the street names.
  • Astana consistently uses this fairly generic design.
  • Zhetisay also uses a fairly generic design, but it is not found in Turkistan or Shymkent.
Yellow boxes connected to the gas pipes are common outside houses in Shymkent, Turkistan, and Taldykorgan.
Turkistan consistently uses these thin grey lamps with two small light sources near the end.
Lamps in Kulsary have a sizable blue photocell on the top.
Some lamps in Uralsk have this very unique design, with 3 separate lamps in an ascending pattern.
East of Aktobe, there is a vertical line of dirt on the right side of the roof.

Coverage in dense baltic pine forests can be found north of Shchuchinsk, which is north of Astana.

NOTE: Baltic pines can be found in other parts of the country.
Parts of Oskemen have hazy forest fire coverage.
In southern Almaty City, there is snow coverage in the mountains.
The Altyn Emel National Park is a barren grassland with snowy mountains in all directions. Some parts are very snowy. And in the eastern section, there is a small curvy mountain pass.
The only May coverage in Kazakhstan is found in the Almaty exclave of Alataou, which is east of Almaty proper. All of the coverage is sunny and the mountains are visible to the south.
A small ridge of hills is visible to the north in a lot of Taldykorgan coverage.
Near the Turkmenistan border in southwest Kazakhstan, you will find this unpaved sandy desert road. The landscape is almost blindingly bright from the sand.

steps.title: Maps and resources
steps.html:
GeoGuessr’s own official maps are not very good, for a variety of reasons. Plonk It recommends the following maps instead:

  • A Diverse Kazakhstan (map link) - The map has over 53,000 locations evenly spread across the country with a good urban/rural balance.

In addition, here are some resources to help you practise Kazakhstan:

  • Plonk It Kazakhstan (map link) - This map contains locations for practising each meta in the Plonk It Kazakhstan guide from step 2 to 3.

lm.name: 6-lane Divided Highway in Autumn
lm.note:
There are two 6-lane divided highways in Kazakhstan that are covered in autumn (image 1):

  1. A1, connecting Astana and Shchuchinsk.
  2. A short stretch of the M-36, connecting Temirtau with Karaganda.

Both roads have 3 lanes in one direction, with coverage in both ways. They are surrounded by green fields with sparsely grown trees (image 2).

You can distinguish them by the meta cars:

Driving south:

  1. A1 is covered by a dirty car without a bracket. The car is blurred near Astana, but this section is perfectly flat, unlike M-36.
  2. M-36 is covered by a car with a bracket.

Driving north:

  1. A1 is covered by a car with a bracket.
  2. M-36 is covered by a car without a bracket.

Note: There is one other non-urban 6-lane divided road in the country, but it was covered in winter.

lm.name: Akkol Car with a Bracket and a Dot Between the Metal Holders – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bracket and a Dot Between the Metal Holders (image 1), you must be in Akkol.

Be careful — a similar dot between metal holders appears in Petropavl, Rudny, and Kostanay, but it’s larger and has a different shape (image 2).

lm.name: Akkol Lamp Post Paint
lm.note: Akkol commonly uses a lamp post paint scheme consisting of a short blue stripe, a long yellow stripe, followed by another short blue stripe, and then yellow extending down to the bottom (image 1).

lm.name: Akmola Region License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for the Akmola Region is 03.

Note: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

lm.name: Akmola Region Pole Paint
lm.note:
In the Akmola Region, poles are occasionally painted with the following scheme: a short red stripe, followed by white, and sometimes black at the bottom (image 1).

Note: Similar poles can also be found in a few villages in southern Kazakhstan.

lm.name: Aktau Car with 2 Faded Dots and 1 Pronounced Dot – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 2 Faded Dots and 1 Pronounced Dot (image 1), you must be in the northern part of Aktau.

lm.name: Aktau Pole-Mounted Street Signs
lm.note:
Street signs in Aktau feature black text on a white background, enclosed in a golden metal frame (image 1). A circle at the top indicates the city district you’re in, and the pointed end directs you toward other districts.

Note: Many districts are labeled on the map, so you can use the information from the sign to find the exact location.

lm.name: Aktau Street Lamps
lm.note:
In Aktau, you can find these thin grey lamp posts with three light sources and a white sticker forming an 'L' shape (image 1).

Note: Similar-looking lamps can be found in other cities as well.

lm.name: Aktobe Buses
lm.note: In Aktobe, you can commonly see these buses with a black and orange color scheme, featuring an orange horizontal line on the side (image 1).

lm.name: Aktobe Car with 2 Faded Dots – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 2 Faded Dots (image 1), you must be in the eastern part of Aktobe.

lm.name: Aktobe Car with 4 Stripes and 2 Smudges – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 4 Stripes and 2 Smudges (image 1), you must be in the western part of Aktobe.

Note: You can confirm it by the presence of a white sticker on the front-left part of the roof.

lm.name: Aktobe Lamp Post Paint
lm.note:
In Aktobe, on some major streets, you can spot lamp posts painted light blue with a yellow stripe at the top (image 1).

I've marked all the streets where I've found them so far (image 2), though there may be more.

lm.name: Aktobe Region License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for the Aktobe Region is 04.

Note: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

lm.name: Aktobe Surface-Mounted Street Signs
lm.note:
In Aktobe, you can often find these street signs attached to fences or buildings, each with a house number inside a circle, where half of the space is occupied by a QR code (image 1).

Be careful — similar signs can be found in Kulsary, but there the house number is not inside a circle (image 2).*

lm.name: Almaty Buses
lm.note:
In Almaty, you can commonly see these green buses with white patterns (image 1).

Be careful — similar buses occasionally appear in Taraz and in Shymkent, but they have a different logo on the side (image 2). Additionally, Shymkent was covered in late spring, Taraz in early spring, while Almaty in autumn and winter.

Generally, if you see more than one bus with this color scheme at the same time, you're most likely in Almaty.

lm.name: Almaty License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for the Almaty is 02.

Note: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

lm.name: Almaty/Jetisu Region License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for the Almaty Region is 05. Jetisu Region officially uses 19, but it was formed in June 2022 by separating from Almaty Region, so in practice, the vast majority of vehicles there still have the Almaty Region code.

Note: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

lm.name: Astana Buses
lm.note:
In Astana, you can commonly see these white buses with a black and green pattern on the side (image 1). Sometimes, the green is replaced with blue.

Be careful not to confuse them with Petropavl buses, which look very similar but lack the black in their color scheme.

If you're unsure which bus you’re seeing, check whether the car has a wire in the top-left part of the truck bed. In Petropavl, the wire is present — in Astana, it's not (image 2).

Note: The wire may look slightly different or might not be visible due to the car blur.

lm.name: Astana License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for Astana is 01.

Note: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

lm.name: Astana Surface-Mounted Street Signs
lm.note:
In Astana, you can find these street signs attached to fences or buildings (image 1). The design is fairly generic, but consistently used across the city.

Note: Spotting a different street sign doesn't rule out Astana.

lm.name: Atbasar Pole Paint
lm.note:
In Atbasar, you can occasionally spot poles painted in a burgundy color with a black stripe at the top (image 1).

Note: This paint scheme is used for poles holding street lamps. Poles without mounted lamps are likely either unpainted or use the Akmola color scheme.

lm.name: Atyrau / Semey Buses
lm.note:
In Atyrau and Semey, you can occasionally spot these light green buses with a white lower section (image 1).

You can distinguish the two cities by the coverage season and car meta:

  • Atyrau was covered in summer, while Semey was covered in autumn.
  • Look for a wire in the top-left part of the truck bed: it is present in Atyrau but absent in Semey (image 2).

Note: The wire may look slightly different or might not be visible due to the car blur.

lm.name: Atyrau Bus Stops
lm.note: In Atyrau, you can commonly see these green and white bus stops with a distinct design (image 1).

lm.name: Atyrau Buses
lm.note:
In Atyrau, you can commonly spot these eco-friendly, gas-powered Yutong buses painted in a light green and white color scheme (image 1).

These buses are also used in other cities across Kazakhstan, but if you can see the side of the bus, you may be able to distinguish it by the Atyrau logo, which is quite recognizable, even from a distance.

Note: Sometimes the bus may be dirty, making the logo less visible.

lm.name: Atyrau Lamp Post Paint
lm.note:
In Atyrau, you can spot lamp posts painted dark green at the base (image 1). Sometimes, there's also a yellow stripe above the green section. These are quite common in the suburbs but they usually don’t appear in the city center.

Note: There’s a good chance that lamp posts in other cities may also be painted in similar colors, so use this clue cautiously.

lm.name: Atyrau Region License Plate Code
lm.note:
In Kazakhstan, you can occasionally spot license plates on the rear of buses and trucks (image 1). The last two digits of a license plate indicate the region of registration.

The area code for the Atyrau Region is 06.

Note 1: Since vehicles often travel between regions, use this clue cautiously. It’s more reliable when seen on local public transport or smaller commercial vehicles than on long-distance trucks.

Note 2: Be careful — in Aktau, you may spot public transport buses with a light green and white color scheme, often covered in advertisements, that use the same 06 code. These buses were most likely registered in Atyrau and later transferred to Aktau but not re-registered due to cost efficiency.

lm.name: Atyrau Region Pole Paint
lm.note:
In the Atyrau Region, poles are painted with blue, white, and black (image 1).

They are most commonly seen in Atyrau city, but also appear occasionally in Kulsary. You can spot them while driving south through Dossor and north through Inderbor as well.

Note: I've seen this pole paint once in Turkistan.

lm.name: Atyrau Traffic Light Poles
lm.note:
Atyrau sometimes uses these ornamental traffic light poles (image 1). You can mostly find them along Sultan Baybarys Avenue in the city center, although they also appear at other major intersections.

Here are all the spots where I've found them so far (image 2), though there may be more.

lm.name: Balkhash Car with 1 Line on the Left and 2 Lines on the Right – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 1 Line on the Left and 2 Lines on the Right (image 1), you must be in the eastern part of Balkhash.

lm.name: Balkhash Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, and 2 Lines on the Right – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, and 2 Lines on the Right (image 1), you must be in the southeastern part of Balkhash.

lm.name: Balkhash Car with a Bracket, a Dot on the Top Left, and a Dirty Back – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bracket, a Dot on the Top Left, and a Dirty Back (image 1), you must be in the eastern part of Balkhash.

Be careful — the same car, but without the dirty back, also appears in Oskemen and Semey. However, the coverage in those cities was done in early autumn, so the surroundings appear much more colorful.

Note: Sometimes the dot is barely visible.

lm.name: Baltic Pine Forests
lm.note:
The roads north of Shchuchinsk around the lakes (image 1), are very distinctive — they are surrounded by Baltic pine forests in hilly terrain (image 2). Sometimes, you’ll even be able to spot lakes behind the trees. The coverage was taken in early August, so the trees are green and the weather is very sunny.

Note: Baltic pines can also be found in other parts of Kazakhstan.

lm.name: Blurred Car in Flat, Dry, Grassy Fields
lm.note:
The section of P27, starting at the intersection north of Maykain and driving northeast up to Shiyli Lake (image 1), is covered by a blurred car.

The landscape is mostly flat, with yellow grassy fields and no trees in sight — though occasionally, small trees with autumn-colored leaves appear. The sky is completely clear, and the sun is visible in the west. The road is in good condition, with grey gravel lining the sides. The southern part of the road is slightly hilly. The overall scenery is illustrated in image 2.

Note: Blurred cars can appear almost anywhere in Kazakhstan, so use this hint with caution.

lm.name: Blurred Car in Flat, Green, Grassy Fields
lm.note:
The section of A-22, starting from Komsomol’skoye and driving northeast to Terensay (image 1), is covered by a blurred car.

The landscape is mostly flat, with grassy green or yellow fields and no trees in sight — except near towns. The sky is filled with grey clouds, though the sun is still visible behind them. The road surface is of medium quality. The overall scenery is illustrated in image 2.

Note: Blurred cars can appear literally anywhere in Kazakhstan, so use this hint with caution.

lm.name: Blurred Car on the Divided Highway in Overcast Weather
lm.note:
The A2 highway, starting in Almaty and driving east past Kaskelen to Zhanakurylys (image 1), is a divided road covered by a blurred car during winter under heavy overcast skies (image 2). The closer you get to Almaty, the more traffic you'll see on the road.

Note: There are other divided highways covered by a blurred car, so use this hint with caution.

lm.name: Blurred Car on the Divided Highway With Trees
lm.note:
The A1 highway, starting just after leaving the suburbs of Shchuchinsk and driving northwest up to the intersection with the exit to Kenesary (image 1), is a divided road covered by a blurred car during autumn. The southern section of the road is lined with trees, and small hills are often visible in the background. As you go north, the trees gradually set back from the road, making the hills more visible. The overall scenery is illustrated in image 2.

Note: There are other divided highways covered by a blurred car, so use this hint with caution.

lm.name: Blurred Car with 2 Stripes on the Divided Highway
lm.note:
The unlabeled road, starting in the suburbs of Turkistan and driving east toward Hazret-Sultan International Airport (image 1), is a divided highway featuring a blurred car with two stripes. The road is quite recognizable thanks to the flat landscape, small crop plantations all around, and sunset coverage (image 2).

Note: Occasionally, the car is unblurred (image 3).

lm.name: Burabay Car with 4 Stripes and Dots in a Line – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and see this Car with 4 Stripes and Dots in a Line (image 1, image 2 — zoomed in), you must be in Burabay.

lm.name: Car Dirty in the Middle
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car Dirty in the Middle (image 2).

  • A3, between the intersection near Ravlekatel'nyy Tsentr Dos and Avtomobil'nyy Most, in both directions.

The stretch of A3 between Almaty and Konaev has three lanes in one direction. The dirt on the roof appears darker and more pronounced when driving north. When driving south, it looks slightly browner and less visible.

Note: The A3 near Konaev is covered by a different car.

lm.name: Car Dirty Vertically on the Left – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car Dirty Vertically on the Left (image 2):

  • A3, starting from the suburbs of Oskemen and driving north up to the intersection west of Shemonaikha.

Near Oskemen, you can see a leaf on the left side of the roof. Around Predgornoje, the leaf disappears.

Note 1: The car is occasionally blurred, but the vertical dirt on the top left is still visible.

Note 2: The same car also appears in Ridder's suburbs, but Ridder has overcast skies, unlike the sunny weather on A3.

lm.name: Car Dirty Vertically on the Left – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car Dirty Vertically on the Left (image 1), you must be in the western suburbs of Ridder.

Note 1: The car is occasionally blurred, but the vertical dirt on the top left is still visible.

Note 2: A similar dirt pattern can be seen on a car in Semey, but that one does not have a bracket, which makes it easy to distinguish.

lm.name: Car Dirty Vertically on the Right
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car Dirty Vertically on the Right (image 2):

  • E38, starting at Aktobe and driving east, then turning to A-22 and continuing northeast up to Komsomol'skoye.

Note: A car driving along A1 from Shchuchinsk to Astana has a similar dirt pattern on the right side, but that road is a divided highway, unlike the routes listed above.

lm.name: Car with 'Lightning' Smudges
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 'Lightning' Smudges (image 2):

  • A-2, starting at Vodokhranilishche Shor-Koo lake, driving southwest up to the intersection with M39, then driving west up to Taraz.

You can distinguish sections of this road by the visibility of the mountains:

  • From Shor-Koo lake to the intersection with M39, you may pass through small hills, but no high mountains are visible to the south.
  • West of the intersection with M39, mountains become visible to the south almost continuously, though they may be hard to spot at times due to thick clouds.

Note 1: Between the intersection with M39 and Kazakh, the car is blurred, but this section can still be recognized by the winter coverage and the presence of a car with 2 stripes and a tilted antenna.

Note 2: This car also appears in western Shymkent, is frequently seen in Taraz, and occasionally appears in Almaty.

lm.name: Car with 'Volcano' Smudge – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 'Volcano' Smudge (image 2):

  • P24, starting at Semey and driving east up to Oskemen.

lm.name: Car with 'Volcano' Smudge – Urban
lm.note: If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 'Volcano' Smudge (image 1), you must be in Oskemen (more likely) or in Semey (less likely).

lm.name: Car with 1 Dot in the Middle
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot in the Middle (image 2):

  1. A1, starting at Kellerovka, driving south to Kokshetau.
  2. A-13, starting at Kokshetau, driving east, then turning south at the intersection near the airport, and continuing up to the intersection with A1.
  3. An unlabeled road, starting at the intersection with A1 and driving east through Akylbay, along with some nearby offroads.

You can distinguish these roads by their driving direction and the surrounding landscape:

  1. Driving more or less south.
  2. Driving east or southeast. You can differentiate the southeast section (which has a similar angle to A1) by the gravel around the road. At A1 it's grey, while on the road near Kokshetau airport it's brown (image 3).
  3. Driving east. From almost every point on the road, you'll be able to see the village and the lake at the foot of a small mountain.

Fun fact: The Partially Blurred 3-Part Car driving on the A1 from Petropavl to Kellerovka also has this dot, but it's not visible. Google blurred the cars completely randomly some time after the coverage was released.

lm.name: Car with 1 Dot on the Left and a Dirty Back
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot on the Left and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  1. A17, starting in the suburbs of Pavlodar and driving southwest up to the intersection near Turgay. A stretch between the intersection northwest of the Сасық көл lake and the intersection with P4 is covered by a different car.
  2. R-174, starting near Karaterek village, driving northwest up to the suburbs of Aksu.

You can distinguish these two sections by the number of roadways:

  1. Divided highway — the farther east you are, the lower the sun is.
  2. Single roadway — the beginning of this coverage is tricky: there’s no visible dot on the left side of the car, but the dirty back part of the roof matches.

Note: On A17, the coverage in the opposite direction was captured with a different car.

lm.name: Car with 1 Dot on the Right
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot on the Right (image 2):

  1. A-2, starting at the intersection with Kb-23, driving east, then turning onto the road north of A-2 through Samsi, returning to A-2, and continuing up to Vodokhranilishche Shor-Koo lake.
  2. A-2, starting at Taraz and driving east, briefly leaving the divided highway to go through Shakbak Baba, and continuing up to Shymkent.

You can distinguish these two sections by landscape and weather:

  1. Up to Kenen, the sky is filled with dark, rainy clouds. On the short stretch of A-2 west of Targap, there is only one roadway. East of Kenen, the landscape becomes flatter, with no sizable hills.
  2. In this section, large hills are visible to the south. The weather is sunny — unlike the A-2 segment near Almaty. Between Taraz and Aisha Bibi, and near Shymkent, there isn’t a single cloud in the sky.

Note: In Shakbak Baba, the lamp posts are painted similar to poles in Taraz, with red, yellow and black stripes.

Note 2: You can also find this car in northeastern Shymkent, southern Taraz, and occasionally in Almaty.

lm.name: Car with 1 Dot on the Top Left
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 1 Dot on the Top Left (image 2):

  • Unlabeled road, starting at the suburbs of Turkistan and driving northeast to Kentau.

Note 1: Don’t confuse this car with a similar one that also has a dot on the top left — that one includes a bracket.

Note 2: You can also find this car in Kentau.

lm.name: Car with 2 Distant Dots
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 2 Distant Dots (image 2):

  • E38, starting at the intersection with the road leading to Aral, driving north up to the intersection with A-26.

Note: The car is generally covered in dirt, but the two marked dots on the roof are more pronounced.

lm.name: Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Left – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Left (image 2):

  • A-16, starting from Zhezquazghan suburbs, driving northwest to Satpayev and from there continuing north up to the Mausoleum of Alasha Khan.

Note: There are other cars with 3 dots but they are not placed in the same configuration.

lm.name: Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Left – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Left (image 1), you must be in Satpayev, a small town north of Zhezqazghan.

Note: There are other cars with 3 dots but they are not placed in the same configuration.

lm.name: Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Right
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 2 Dots in the Middle and 1 on the Right (image 2):

  1. R-69, starting from the suburbs of Kyzylorda and driving northwest up to Josaly.
  2. E38, between Sunakata and Turkistan, covered in both directions.

You can distinguish these two roads by the number of roadways:

  1. Single roadway.
  2. Divided highway.

Note 1: The car gets blurred a few kilometers north of Karaketken and becomes unblurred before reaching the water reservoir east of Josaly.

Note 2: There are other cars with 3 dots, but they are placed in different configurations.

lm.name: Car with 2 Dots on the Left and 1 on the Right
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 2 Dots on the Left and 1 on the Right (image 2):

  • M-36, starting at a couple of kilometers north of Kurty, driving southeast up to the intersection with P-19, turning southwest and continuing up to the south suburbs of Shamalgan.

Coverage was captured during sunset — the farther south you go, the darker it gets. This section also has a distinct late autumn vibe, and, unlike the northern parts of the route, has no parallel road under construction, except for a very short section north of Kurty.

Note 1: If you see this car in an urban environment, you're passing through Shamalgan.

Note 2: The car appears blurred near Lake Sorbulaq.

lm.name: Car with 2 Lines on the Left – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 2 Lines on the Left (image 2):

  1. E38, between Shymkent and Turkistan, with the car leaving the road only to bypass Temirlanovka. The road is covered in both directions.
  2. A-2, starting at the exit to Kumaryk, driving east, then taking an exit and continuing along the road south of A-2. At the intersection with R-39, the car turns north and returns to A-2, continuing its journey east. It then exits again at the intersection with M39 and drives further east up to the Kyrgyzstan border.
  3. A-2, starting at the intersection near Kenen, driving south up to Alga (where the car gets blurred), passing through Korday, and continuing via Өтеген көшесі to the intersection with Ob"Yezdnaya Doroga, where the car becomes visible again and proceeds east to the Kara-Su suburbs.

You can distinguish these three sections by driving direction and the sun:

  1. Driving southeast or northeast on a divided highway. The smudge on the left side extends into the middle of the roof (top part of image 2).
  2. Mostly driving east with the sun high in the sky. The smudge on the left is shorter and does not extend into the middle like on E38 (bottom part of image 2). If the car is not on A-2, it often passes through villages where you can spot various differently painted poles.
  3. Driving south, then briefly east. There’s no extended smudge (bottom part of image 2). The A2 section between Kenen and Korday has a distinct grainy, “salt and pepper” texture (image 3). The car is blurred in the middle of this section, but the road is still easy to recognize — grassy fields with rows of trees planted along the road, “Turkish” pavement, and the distinctive sunset coverage.

Note: The same car also covered some roads in Shymkent, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with 2 Lines on the Left – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 2 Lines on the Left (image 1), you must be in the northwestern part of Shymkent.

Note 1: The same car also covered some major highways, which occasionally pass through urban areas, so take that into account.

Note 2: A car with similar lines appears in Kostanay, but it has 4 stripes and a white sticker, unlike the one in Shymkent (image 2).

lm.name: Car with 2 Small Dots on the Bottom Left
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 2 Small Dots on the Bottom Left (image 2):

  • M-36, starting at Atbasar and driving east to Astana.

These dots are sometimes barely visible. The same dots are present on the Car with Orange Smudge on the Right, but apart from these 2, there will be some additional ones and, most of the time, a visible orange smudge on the right side.

Note: Occasionally, you can also confirm this car by spotting an orange bag in the trunk, though it’s not always visible (image 3).

lm.name: Car with 2 Small Dots on the Left
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 2 Small Dots on the Left (image 2):

  1. P34, starting at the intersection with A17 and driving south to Karazhal.
  2. A17, starting at the intersection with P34 and driving east up to the roundabout in Atasu.
  3. Unlabeled road, starting at Doskey, driving east, then north up to Botakara, passing through the town, then continuing east via Karagana-Karkaralinsk road up to Karkaraly.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction, landscape, and time of day:

  1. Driving southeast through flat desert. It’s very sunny, and the dots on the car are hard to spot.
  2. Driving east at sunset. The farther east you go, the lower the sun is.
  3. Up to Botakara, the car is driving east and north. The sun is high in the sky, unlike on A17. From Botakara the car heads southeast, but the terrain features rolling hills, unlike the flat landscape of P34.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and a Tilted Antenna Among Hills
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 4 Stripes and a Tilted Antenna (image 2):

  • A9, starting at Sekisovka and driving east up to Ridder.

This road is quite recognizable, due to the autumn coverage, surrounding hills, and nice weather.

Note: You can find the car with 4 stripes and tilted antenna on other roads, but the landscape there is not as hilly.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and a Tilted Antenna in Cloudy Weather
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 4 Stripes and a Tilted Antenna (image 2):

  1. M-36, starting just north of Chaltas, driving southeast up to a point about 30 km north of Balkhash, where the coverage ends due to sunset. The remaining stretch was covered from the intersection with R-181, driving north until it reconnects with the previously mentioned section (right part of image 1).
  2. M-36, starting at the intersection with A-358 and driving southeast up to Kurtyt.

You don’t really need car meta to recognize the M-36, as it is highly distinctive. The second road is under construction for most of its length, and the coverage was done during late autumn, making the barren landscape appear brown and lifeless.

You can distinguish between the two sections by the appearance of the clouds:

  1. In the first section, clouds are thin and evenly spread across the sky, except in the southernmost part where the coverage was done driving north under very sunny conditions.
  2. In the northern parts of the second section, clouds are dense and the sun is not visible. As you move south, the sky clears up, and the clouds become puffier and densely packed.

Note 1: The car is often blurred, but the two front stripes are always visible. Other segments of the road were covered by cars without visible stripes.

Note 2: There are other roads covered by the car with 4 stripes and a tilted antenna, but they lack a parallel road under construction and the coverage was done in early autumn.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and a White Sticker in the Desert
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 4 Stripes and a White Sticker (image 2):

  1. A-28, starting at Atyrau and driving north up to Tinali.
  2. A-27, starting at Zhanterek and driving southwest up to Dossor.
  3. A-33, starting at Dossor and driving south up to Beyneu.
  4. M32, starting at Josaly and driving northwest up to Uindu.
  5. M32, between Kyzylorda to Sunakata, covered in both directions.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction, weather, number of roadways and car meta:

  1. Driving north. There are many clouds in the sky (on M32, driving in a similar direction, there are either none or only a few small ones). Up to Inderbor, the weather is mostly sunny, moving north the sky becomes overcast, and near Tinali, the sun is setting. This section is also greener than the rest.
  2. Driving southwest. Unlike M32, which has no clouds, A-27 has a few. The car is also noticeably dirty at the back.
  3. Driving south. M32 driving in a similar direction is divided, while A-33 is not. The weather is very sunny starting at Dossor, becoming cloudier the further south you go.
  4. Driving northeast on a single roadway, unlike the divided M32 below Kyzylorda. The car also has the additional dot on the left side (image 3).
  5. The only divided highway covered by this car.

Note 1: The same car can also be found in the northern, greener parts of Kazakhstan, as well as in urban areas and the suburbs of larger cities.

Note 2: The sticker may be hard to see, especially on the southern roads, but you can still recognize it by the slightly sharp-looking top-left edge of the car.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and a White Sticker in the Green Plains
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 4 Stripes and a White Sticker (image 2):

  1. Орал-Самара жолы road, starting from Uralsk and driving north up to the Russian border.
  2. A-32, starting from Uralsk and driving north up to the Russian border.
  3. E38, starting from Uralsk and driving southeast through Zhympity, then continuing east up to Kobda.
  4. A-22, starting at Livanovka, driving north around Antonovka, then heading northeast up to Rudny.
  5. A-21, starting from Kostanay and driving northeast up to Ukatkan.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction, weather, and car blur.

  1. Coverage on this road was done during overcast weather, and the car is blurred (only 2 stripes and the sticker are visible). A blurred car driving in a similar direction appears also on A-22 near Livanovka, but the weather there is sunny. If you see a long line of trucks, you're very close to the border with Russia.
  2. Car is fully visible, driving north under overcast skies — this combination is unique to this stretch.
  3. Driving southeast, then east. The section has consistent cloud cover, unlike other eastbound roads. Around Kulzhabay, the pavement becomes wet. The car is blurred in some parts.
  4. Driving northeast during sunset. The car is blurred in the first half of this section. Near Rudny, you can spot a second roadway under construction.
  5. Also driving northeast, but the sun is higher. This stretch has noticeably more tree cover compared to the others.

Note: The same car can also be found in the southwestern, desert regions of Kazakhstan, as well as in urban areas and the suburbs of larger cities.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and Several Dots – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 4 Stripes and Several Dots (image 2):

  • R-174, starting near Karaterek village and driving southeast up to Chagan.

There are no particularly distinctive dots or smudges on the roof — you’ll need to learn the general pattern to recognize it.

The coverage was captured during sunset — the farther south you go, the darker it becomes. If the car is driving northeast through a semi-urban area, you may be in Kurchatov.

Note 1: The same car also covered some roads in Oskemen, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account. However, the version of this car on R-174 has a tilted antenna, so if you see this car with an 8-stripe antenna, you're not on R-174.

Note 2: The antenna is not always visible.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes and Several Dots – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and see this Car with 4 Stripes and Several Dots (image 1), you must be in the northeastern part of Pavlodar.

There are no particularly distinctive dots or smudges on the roof — you’ll need to learn the general pattern to recognize it.

Note: The same car also covered the road that passes through Kurchatov, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back - Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  • M38, starting at Semey and driving southeast up to Qalbatau.

Note 1: The same car also appears on the A3 between Qalbatau and Oskemen, but it is driving northeast, and the sun is noticeably lower compared to M38.

Note 2: The antenna is not always visible.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back at Sunset – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  • A3, starting at Qualbatau and driving northeast up to Oskemen.

This road is easily recognizable due to the sunset coverage. The pavement is in very good condition, and the farther east you go, the lower the sun appears in the sky.

Note 1: The same car also appears on the M-38 between Semey and Qalbatau, but it is driving southeast, and the sun is noticeably higher compared to A3.

lm.name: Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted antenna, a Dirty Back, and a Bird Poop
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted antenna, a Dirty Back, and a Bird Poop (image 2):

  1. P27, starting at Korneevka and driving southwest to Botakara, then turning onto Karaganda–Karkaralinsk road and continuing up to the intersection with A17.
  2. A short stretch of P27 south of Bayanaul, driving west. The town of Bayanaul itself is also covered by this car.
  3. R-174, starting at the suburbs of Semey and driving west up to Chagan.

You can distinguish these roads by the surrounding landscape and weather:

  1. The terrain is fairly flat, and the weather is cloudy. The car becomes blurred halfway between Botakara and Sartobe.
  2. The road is surrounded by small hills with exposed rocks, and the sun is high in the sky. While the car may appear blurred in Bayanaul, the coverage is easily recognizable thanks to the hilly terrain and the distinct late-autumn scenery.
  3. The landscape is extremely flat, and there isn’t a single cloud in the sky.

Note: Sometimes the antenna is not visible.

lm.name: Car with 6 Dots – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 6 Dots (image 2):

  • Unlabeled road, starting at the intersection with A17 near Tortkuduk, driving east to R-174, then continuing north and eventually returning to A17.

The car is blurred near Aksu and on the final straight stretch leading back to A17, but even in these sections, you can still recognise it by the dirt dots on the front left side and a smudge on the right (image 3).

Note: The same car was used in Pavlodar, which you might occasionally confuse with R-174, as some parts of R-174 near larger towns can resemble an urban area. You can distinguish it from Pavlodar by the fact that the dots are more faded on R-174 (image 4).

lm.name: Car with 6 Dots – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 6 Dots (image 1), you must be in Pavlodar.

Note: The same car also covers R-174, which in some spots near larger towns may resemble an urban area. However, you can distinguish it from Pavlodar by the fact that the dots are more faded (image 2).

lm.name: Car with a Bird Poop on the Left – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bird Poop on the Left (image 1, marked with a red circle), you must be in the eastern part of Kulsary, northern part of Zhanaozen, or (rarely) northern part of Aktobe.

You can distinguish between these cities by the presence of additional bird poop (marked with a blue circle in image 1) and the surrounding landscape:

  • Zhanaozen — No additional bird poop; the environment is desert-like.
  • Kulsary — Additional bird poop is present; also features a desert-like landscape.
  • Aktobe — Additional bird poop is often (but not always) visible; the surroundings are noticeably greener than in the other two cities.

lm.name: Car with a Black Dot and a White Dot
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Black Dot and a White Dot (image 2):

  • M-38, starting at Pavlodar and driving southeast up to Semey.

Near Pavlodar, the white dot is less visible. The farther south you go, the lower the sun appears in the sky.

Note: The white dot appears on other roads as well, but not together with the black one.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and 5 Dots
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Bracket and 5 Dots (image 2):

  • M38, in the suburbs of Pavlodar and driving northwest up to the Russian border.

The coverage on this road was done during sunrise, so the farther north you go, the higher the sun appears in the sky.

A short stretch of the road near Pavlodar is divided, and coverage was captured in both directions.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder (image 2):

  1. A17, starting east of the intersection above Abay and driving northeast up to Karaganda.
  2. A17, starting at the same location and driving south and then southwest up to Atasu.

You can distinguish these sections by driving direction, number of traffic lanes, and landscape:

  1. Driving northwest. The road has two lanes in one direction for the most of its length. It is frequently traveled by cars, and the closer you are to Karaganda, the heavier the traffic.
  2. Driving south or southwest. The road has only one lane per direction, except for a very short stretch near Abay. The car is often blurred, but you can still recognise this road by the surrounding landscape (image 3):
  • The weather is very sunny, with not a single cloud in the sky.
  • The terrain is slightly hilly, or you can see small hills in the distance. Sometimes the elevation changes are minimal, but it’s almost never completely flat.
  • The grass is dry and yellowish, with no large trees — only small bushes.

The same car with the poop on the metal holder also appears in Karaganda, its suburbs (including Saran), and Kokshetau, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and see this Car with a Bracket and Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder (image 1), you must be in Karaganda, its suburbs (including Saran), or Kokshetau.

You can distinguish Kokshetau from the other locations by the appearance of the bird poop, which is less pronounced than in the Karaganda area (image 2).

Note: The same car also covered A17 between Karaganda and Atasu, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dirty Back
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  1. A-27, starting in the suburbs of Aktobe, driving south through Kandyagash, then continuing via A-26 up to midway between Izembet and Dzhurun.
  2. A-27, starting in Kandyagash and driving southwest up to Zharly.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction:

  1. Driving south. Additionally, many sections of the A-27 feature a parallel road under construction.
  2. Driving southwest.

Note: If you're driving southwest through an urban area, you're likely in Kandyagash.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dot Between the Metal Holders – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bracket and a Dot Between the Metal Holders (image 1), you must be in Petropavl, the southern part of Rudny, or the western suburbs of Kostanay.

Be careful — a similar dot between metal holders appears in Akkol, but it’s smaller and has a different shape (image 2).

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left (image 2):

  • A322, starting at Semey, driving northeast, then turning east on P-147 to Shemonaikha and then continuing via A3 (or an unlabeled road) to the intersection with A-9, before finally heading south to Oskemen.

You can distinguish these sections by driving direction, cloud coverage, and sun position.

Near Semey, the weather is quite cloudy. Around Novaya Suhl'ba, the sky becomes almost completely clear. The closer you get to Oskemen, the lower the sun is in the sky.

Note: There is another road covered by the car with the dot on the top left, but it has a parallel road under construction, and the coverage was done in late autumn.

Bonus: If you see this car driving through a city and there are street lamps with three square light sources along the road (image 3), you're in Shemonaikha.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left (image 1), you must be in Semey or Oskemen.

In Oskemen, this car sometimes has a dirty roof (image 2). You can find both versions of the car in the northwestern part of the city, while the one with the dirty roof also appears in the southeastern suburbs.

Be careful — a car with the same dot but with a dirty back also appears in Balkhash. However, the coverage in that city was done in late autumn, so the surroundings appear much more brownish and lifeless.

Note: Sometimes the dot is barely visible.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Small Dot on the Right
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Small Dot on the Right (image 2):

  • A24, starting in the suburbs of Aktobe and driving northwest up to the Russian Border.

Be careful not to confuse the marked dot with the dots visible below, which were caused by roof damage (along with the scratch) and appear in many different locations across Kazakhstan.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Tilted Antenna – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by Car with a Bracket and a Tilted Antenna (image 2):

  1. Unlabeled road, starting at the Shanyrak roundabout in Uralsk, driving west to the intersection with E38, then continuing up to the Russian border.
  2. A-28, starting at the intersection near Tinali and driving north up to Uralsk suburbs.
  3. E38, starting in Kobda and driving west up to Aktobe suburbs.

You can distinguish these three sections by driving direction:

  1. Driving west.
  2. Driving north.
  3. Driving east. The road between Kurashasay and Aktobe is divided.

Note 1: Sometimes the antenna is not visible.

Note 2: The same car also covered some roads in Uralsk and Aktobe, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a Tilted Antenna – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Bracket and a Tilted Antenna (image 1), you must be either in Uralsk, Aktobe, or Kobda.

You can easily distinguish Kobda, as it has coverage only along the main road, where you’ll notice distinct utility poles painted with two stripes — red and yellow — followed by light blue extending to the bottom (image 2).

Note: The same car also covered some major highways around Uralsk, which occasionally passes close to urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket and a White Dot – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and see this Car with a Bracket and a White Dot (image 1), you must be in Pavlodar (more likely) or the western suburbs of Semey (less likely).

There is no meta that is 100% reliable for distinguishing these cities, but here are some tips:

  • The dot in Pavlodar is more pronounced and easier to spot than in Semey (image 2).
  • Most of the coverage in Pavlodar was captured on sunny days, while in Semey it is usually very cloudy or the sun is completely obscured.
  • This car only covered small roads in the suburbs of Semey, so if you are on a wider, major road and see buildings that are not family cottages, you are most likely in Pavlodar.

Note: The dot is sometimes barely visible or appears black instead.

lm.name: Car with a Bracket, a Dot on the Top Left, and a Dirty Back – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket, a Dot on the Top Left, and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  1. Unlabeled divided highway, starting at the intersection with Km-15 (south of Ushtobe), driving southwest to M36, and continuing south almost up to Chaltas.
  2. M-36, starting at the intersection with R-181 (northwest of Balkhash), driving south along the eastern shore of Lake Balkhash up to the intersection with A-358.

You don’t really need car meta to recognize the M-36, as it is highly distinctive. The second road is under construction for most of its length, and the coverage was captured during late autumn, making the barren landscape appear brown and lifeless.

You can distinguish between the two sections by weather and driving direction:

  1. Driving briefly southwest, then south or southeast. The sky is cloudy, especially in the southern part of this section, but the sun is visible. From the intersection with Km-15 to the one east of Novostrojka, the road is a divided highway with wet pavement (image 3), as the car began driving shortly after a rainfall. Further south, the second roadway is under construction. The car briefly leaves the M36 a couple of kilometers south of Novostrojka, passes through Kurminskoe, and rejoins the M36 at the intersection in Zhumabek.
  2. Driving southwest, then southeast. Even when the direction is similar to section 1, the weather is noticeably different — it’s fully overcast and the sun is not visible.

Additionally, this car covers the road driving north from Balkhash to the airport.

Note 1: The car may be blurred, but the dot on the top left should still be visible.

Note 2: There is another road covered by the car with the dot on the top left, but it lacks a parallel road under construction, and the coverage was done in early autumn.

lm.name: Car with a Dirty Back – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Dirty Back (image 1), you must be either in Oskemen or Ridder.

In Ridder it is always very cloudy and mountainous, while in Oskemen most of the coverage was done during sunny days and the hills are much smaller.

Note: There are several dirty cars, but the smudge patterns vary — be careful not to confuse them.

lm.name: Car with a Dot on the Front
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Dot on the Front (image 2):

  • A-17, starting at the intersection north of Ekibastuz, driving northeast up to Pavlodar.

The farther east you go, the lower the sun is in the sky.

lm.name: Car with a Dot on the Left and on the Right
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Dot on the Left and on the Right (image 2):

  • P-3, starting at the suburbs of Astana and driving south to the eastern suburbs of Koschi. On the divided section of the road, coverage was captured in both directions. The short stretch marked with a red line on the map is covered by a car with 4 stripes and a tilted antenna.

The car was driving south in overcast weather. On the return trip north to Astana, the coverage was done during sunset.

Note: You can also find this car in the suburbs of Koschi.

lm.name: Car with a Faded Dot – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Faded Dot (image 2):

  • A-33, starting at the Aisha Bibi café-hotel near Say-Otes and driving northeast up to Beyneu.

Driving northeast through the desert is quite distinctive for this road.

Note 2: The same car also covered some roads in Aktau, Zhanaozen and Kulsary, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Faded Dot – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Faded Dot (image 1), you must be in the southeastern part of Aktau, southern part of Zhanaozen, or occasionally in the southern part of Kulsary.

In Kulsary, the car often has a dirty rear window, unlike in Aktau and Zhanaozen — but this is not a fully reliable meta.

Note 1: The dot may be hard to see under intense sunlight.

Note 2: The same car also covered the A-33 between Say-Otes and Beyneu, which occasionally passes close to urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with a Smudge on the Window – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Smudge on the Window (image 1), you must be either in Zhezqazghan or Karazhal.

Note 1: The dirt on the rear window is sometimes barely visible.

Note 2: The same car appears on P-34 and A-17 near Karazhal, but these roads do not pass through any cities.

lm.name: Car with a Wire, a Bracket, a Scratch, and a Dot – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and see this Car with a Wire, a Bracket, a Scratch, and a Dot (image 1), you must be in Esil or Atbasar.

In the northern parts of Atbasar, the roof of the car is very dirty, which can make identifying this car really difficult (image 2).

Note: There may be other cars with a similar dot, so use this clue with caution.

lm.name: Car with a Wire, a Bracket, and a Dot on the Top Right
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Wire, a Bracket and a Dot on Top Right (image 2):

  1. An unlabeled road west of Pavlodar, starting at the intersection with A-12, driving west, then turning northwest at the intersection with A-21 near Pokrovka, and continuing up to the Russian border.
  2. A-12, starting at the intersection west of Pavlodar and driving north up to the border with Russia.

You can distinguish these two roads by driving direction:

  1. West or northwest.
  2. North of northeast.

lm.name: Car with a Wire, a Bracket, and a Slightly Dirty Roof at the Back
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Wire, a Bracket, and a Slightly Dirty Roof at the Back (image 2):

  • The unlabeled road, starting in the suburbs of Petropavl and driving east to the Russian border.

Note: You can confirm this road by the presence of a black box placed in the truck bed, touching the right side panel (image 3).

lm.name: Car with an Orange Smudge on the Right – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with an Orange Smudge on the Right (image 2 — red circle):

  1. R-87, starting at Aleksandrovka and driving northeast up to the Russian border.
  2. R-265, starting at Kostanay, driving south to the intersection with R-263, then continuing east up to Esil.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction and car meta:

  1. Driving northeast. The car has 3 small dots on the right (top part of image 2 — green circle). It is blurred from Aktobe to Aleksandrovka, but if you suspect you’re on this road, check for a small dot just above the blur on the left side of the car (image 3).
  2. Driving southeast or east. The car has 4 small dots on the right (bottom part of image 2 — green circle). Additionally, there are two black smudges on the left rear side of the car (bottom part of image 2 — blue circle). These smudges are clearly visible near Kostanay but become harder to spot the farther you get from the city. This section is quite long, so it's useful to know how to region-guess it:
    • Kostanay–Auliekol stretch: The farther south you go, the higher the sun appears in the sky, and the cloudier it gets.
    • Auliekol–Atbasar stretch: Around Buzuluk, the sun is positioned directly to the south. West of that point, the sun shifts more to the east; east of that point, the opposite happens. You can verify this by facing the camera directly toward the sun (image 4).

Note 1: Sometimes the sun is so bright that the orange smudge is difficult to see, but the black dots on the left should still be visible.

Note 2: The same car also covered some roads in Aktobe, Rudny and Kostanay, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with an Orange Smudge on the Right – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with an Orange Smudge on the Right (image 1), you must be in eastern Aktobe, northeastern Rudny or northeastern Kostanay.

There is a second variant of this smudge, which appears as a leaf stuck in the same spot (middle part of image 1) — this version is only found in Aktobe. Most likely, the leaf fell off while driving, leaving behind the orange smudge.

In Rudny and Kostanay, the car also has additional smudges on the left (bottom part of image 1), which are not present in Aktobe.

Note: This car also covered some major highways that occasionally pass near urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with Labeled Metal Holders – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with Labeled Metal Holders (image 2):

  1. Unlabeled road north of Konaev, starting at the intersection with A3 (Avtomobil'nyy Most), driving north to the intersection near Kirbulak Grocery, turning onto the unpaved off-road, and continuing east to Ile River, and then driving north along the river into the middle of nowhere.
  2. A3, starting at the intersection west of Saryozek, driving north, up to the latitude of Tauracy (a small town located east of A3).

You can distinguish these roads by their driving direction and number of roadways:

  1. A single paved road, driving north. After turning onto the unpaved off-road, you first pass through flat grasslands (top part of image 3), and as you approach the Ile River, the terrain becomes hilly (bottom part of image 3). The car becomes blurred at the end of this section, but the distinct landscape should help you recognize it.
  2. A divided highway.

lm.name: Car with Labeled Metal Holders – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with Labeled Metal Holders (image 1), you're likely in one of the following cities:

  • The southeastern suburbs of Shymkent (very common)
  • The northern part of Taraz (common)
  • The eastern part of Kaskelen (common)
  • Almaty (rare)
  • Taldykorgan (common)

While this meta isn’t especially practical due to the large distances between these cities and the fact that stronger clues are often available in a round, it's still worth learning — especially when you're just starting out and haven’t fully mastered seasonal coverage.

You can distinguish these cities by vegetation and the season:

  • Shymkent – Late spring: bright green grass, trees starting to grow leaves.
  • Taraz – Early spring: grass just turning green, trees still without leaves.
  • Kaskelen – Winter: brown grass and leafless trees. The car shows faint fingerprint marks in the dirt on the roof (image 2).
  • Almaty – Winter: looks like Kaskelen, but the car lacks any distinctive marks.
  • Taldykorgan – Winter: also similar to Kaskelen and Almaty, but you'll often see patches of snow on the ground.

lm.name: Car with Numerous Grey Dots – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with Numerous Grey Dots (image 2):

  • Unlabeled road, starting at Lesbek Batyr and driving south to the Uzbekistan border.

The coverage was captured during sunny weather with a completely clear sky. The landscape is barren, with only sparse grass.

Note: The same car also covered some roads in Zhetisay and Turkistan, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with Numerous Grey Dots – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with Numerous Grey Dots (image 1), you must be in the eastern part of Zhetisay (more likely) or in Turkistan (less likely).

You can distinguish these two cities by the appearance of the dirt on the bottom-left metal holder (image 2).

Note: This car also covered the unlabeled road between Lesbek Batyr and the Uzbekistan border, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with Several Barely Visible Dots on the Right – Non-Urban
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with Several Barely Visible Dots on the Right (image 2):

  1. A17, starting from Kyzylorda and driving northeast until the road closure caused by construction.
  2. An unlabeled road, starting in the suburbs of Turkistan and driving south to Talapty.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction and car meta:

  1. Driving northeast. The car on this road has a black box placed on the truck bed, touching the right side panel (image 3).
  2. Driving southwest or southeast. On the southern stretch of this road, a parallel roadway is under construction.

Note 1: The dots on the car may be difficult to see at times due to intense sunlight.

Note 2: The same car also covered some roads in Kyzylorda, Turkistan and Zhetisay, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.

lm.name: Car with Several Barely Visible Dots on the Right – Urban
lm.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with Several Barely Visible Dots on the Right (image 1), you must be either in Kyzylorda, Turkistan or Zhetisay.

The dots can be hard to spot, especially under intense sunlight.

Note: While this meta isn’t particularly useful, it can at least help rule out cities in the western part of the country, which might look similar.

lm.name: Car with Several Dots on the Left
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with Several Dots on the Left (image 2):

  • A-27, starting at Dossor and driving southwest up to Atyrau.

The road drives among the desert and the weather is very sunny.

lm.name: Car with some Orange Dirt in the Bottom Left
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with some Orange Dirt in the Bottom Left (image 2):

  2. E-121, starting from a random offroad section near the intersection with R-114, driving north, then entering a divided highway and continuing a few kilometers west.

You can distinguish these two sections by the surrounding environment and the position of the sun:

  1. In this section, you can see buildings to the west or north. This coverage was done during the sunset.
  2. This road is surrounded by empty deserts and the sun is high.

Note: On the A33, near Aktau, the Partly Blurred 3-Part Car also appears.

lm.name: Clean Car with 4 Stripes and a Barely Visible Dot on the Right
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with 4 Stripes and a Barely Visible Dot on the Right (image 2):

  1. P4, starting at Astana, driving northeast, then east up to Ekibastuz.
  2. An unlabeled road, driving southeast from Ekibastuz, then entering P27 and continuing south up to Korneevka.
  3. A short stretch of P27 south of Kalkaman.

You can distinguish these roads by number of roadways and driving direction:

  1. Divided highway.
  2. Single roadway. Never driving north or east. Near Bayanau the car is blurred, but you should be able to recognise this road, due to hilly terrain and sunny weather.
  3. Single roadway as well, but the car is driving northeast, north, or east.

Note: The dot on the right is sometimes hard to spot.

lm.name: Clean Car with a Bracket on the Divided Highway in the Green Plains
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with a Bracket (image 2):

  1. A1, starting at the intersection near Kenesary and driving north up to the intersection just south of Ivanovka, where the divided highway ends.
  2. P-10, starting at the intersection with M-36 and circling around the eastern side of Astana up to the intersection near Astana International Airport.
  3. M-36, starting at Astana suburbs and driving southeast up to Temirtau.

The car on these roads has no visible dots, smudges, or other marks. The coverage was done in early autumn.

You can distinguish these two roads by driving direction, weather and car meta:

  1. Driving north under cloudy conditions, but the sun is still visible.
  2. Sunny weather with sparse clouds. The car in this section has visible scratches on the back.
  3. Driving southeast under overcast skies, with the sun not visible at all.

Note: The same clean car can appear on other divided highways near larger cities, so use this clue with caution.

lm.name: Clean Car with a Bracket on the Divided Highway in Winter
lm.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Clean Car with a Bracket (image 2):

  • Divided highway between Saryozek and Taldykorgan (both directions).

This road is unique because, unlike other divided highways that were covered during winter, the car is almost perfectly clean.

Note 1: A small stretch of the road driving north from Taldykorgan is covered by a different car.

Note 2: The same clean car can appear on other divided highways near larger cities, so use this clue with caution.

lm.name: Clean Car with a Small Dot
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with a Small Dot (image 2):

  • A3, starting at Taldykorgan, driving northeast to the intersection with P-130, then changing direction and driving southeast up to Druzhba.

This car is unique, because it is very clean, unlike others used during winter on major roads.

You can distinguish different sections of this route based on driving direction and some other clues:

  • From Taldykorgan to the intersection east of Qyzylagash, there's a second roadway under construction.
  • Between the intersection and the area around Inbek, an off-road track runs parallel to the main road on the north side (except when driving south of Zhansügirov).
  • On the P-130 segment, you're driving alongside large mountains clearly visible to the south.

Note: The car is blurred arround the intersection with A-354.

lm.name: Clean Car with a Wire
lm.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with a Wire (image 2):

  1. E38, starting at Uindu and driving north up to Aral.
  2. A-27, starting at Zharly and driving southwest up to Zhanterek.
  3. A-22, starting at Terensay and driving north up to Livanovka.
  4. R-278, starting at Rudny, driving northeast, turning north at the intersection with Қостанай Западная Обход, continuing around Kostanay, then turning northwest at the intersection with M-36, and finally leaving the road at Fyodorovka and finishing the journey at Kopychenka.
